## Executive Summary

Every day, {{< var global_disease_deaths_daily_nounit >}} people die from diseases humanity spends {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} times more on wars, genocides, and blowing people up than researching. Your governments burn {{< var political_dysfunction_global_opportunity_cost_total >}} a year on [political dysfunction](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd) [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]. This proposal: do 1% less of that. Redirect 1% of military spending to clinical trials. Everything below is the mechanism for making it happen and the math on what changes if it does.

Nobody loses by playing. The only losing move is not playing. The upside/downside ratio is {{< var sharing_upside_downside_ratio_treaty >}}.

Every person alive is {{< var treaty_personal_upside_blend >}} richer in a world that stops wasting {{< var political_dysfunction_global_opportunity_cost_total >}}/year on [political dysfunction](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd). Getting there requires some people to put money in a pool and everyone else to click a button on a website. The upside is {{< var treaty_personal_upside_blend >}}. The downside is {{< var sharing_opportunity_cost >}} of your time. {{< var global_disease_deaths_daily_nounit >}} people die every day while your species sits out a Game it cannot lose.

This chapter explains why, and then explains how.

1. **The Game you're building.** An open-source coordination game: raise global median income and healthy life years within {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}} years.
2. **How you keep score.** At year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}: did people live {{< var treaty_hale_gain_year_15 >}} longer? Did they earn {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_multiplier >}} as much? (See [GDP Trajectories](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025].) That is {{< var treaty_personal_upside_blend >}} per person.
3. **How PRIZE works.** You fund one pool until year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}. Targets missed: you divide the realized pool pro rata.
4. **How VOTE works.** You recruit one verified referendum participant, you earn one point. Targets met: the pool routes to VOTE point-holders.
5. **How you start.** Find a host to launch the [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd). PRIZE deposits begin, the Scoreboard goes live, and recruitment compounds from there. (For the institutional deployment plan, see [Why Your Institution Should Be The Initiating Node](initiating-node-memo.qmd).)
6. **Why you bother.** "Do nothing" is not free. Your governments already waste {{< var political_dysfunction_tax_per_person_annual >}} per person per year ([Political Dysfunction Tax](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd) [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]). The [destructive economy](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] hits 50% of GDP in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}} (the point where half of everything gets looted as fast as it is created).

## How It Works (The 90-Second Version)

**Here's how PRIZE deposits work.** Your deposit goes into a single pool that compounds through the [wishocratic fund](../economics/wishocratic-investment-fund.qmd). Rich people have a secret money club (venture capital and private equity) that makes {{< var venture_gross_return >}} returns. Your retirement account is legally banned from joining. The pool gets you in. It spreads your money across the entire sector so no single bad bet kills you, and crowds pick the investments ({{< var crowd_decision_accuracy >}} accuracy) instead of expensive fund managers ({{< var expert_decision_accuracy >}} accuracy) [@surowiecki-2004]. Result: {{< var prize_pool_annual_return >}} annually, nearly triple conventional retirement at {{< var conventional_retirement_return >}} (see [Wishocratic Investment Fund](../economics/wishocratic-investment-fund.qmd) for the full derivation).

Your deposit is locked. Not a savings account. It stays in your verified account until resolution. Targets missed: you divide the realized pool pro rata. Targets met: the pool goes to VOTE point-holders, not back to you. See the [prize protocol](../appendix/earth-optimization-prize-protocol.qmd) [@earth-optimization-prize-protocol-paper-2025] for the full specification.

**Here's how VOTE points work.** You recruit one verified referendum participant into the first [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025] vote, you earn one point. Points stay with the account that earned them - not tradable, so coalition credit stays with recruiters, not speculators. Registration asks two questions: (1) yes or no on the 1% Treaty (the smallest serious test of whether humans will redirect even 1% from weapons to medicine), and (2) how much military vs. clinical trials, with [Optimitron](../solution/optimocracy.qmd) [@optimocracy-paper-2025] evidence. Fits on a phone. Under a minute.

| Year-15 objective | Current baseline | Year-15 target |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Global HALE** | {{< var global_hale_current >}} | {{< var treaty_projected_hale_year_15 >}} (+{{< var treaty_hale_gain_year_15_nounit >}} healthy years) |
| **Global median income** | {{< var current_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} (status quo at year 15) | {{< var treaty_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} ({{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_multiplier >}} current lifetime earnings; see [GDP Trajectories](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd)) |

Your public signal is the **Scoreboard**, updated in real time: global median HALE, global median income, number of votes, percent support for the 1% Treaty, current wishocratic allocation between military and clinical trials, and size of the PRIZE pool. Polls are ignorable. Petitions are ignorable. A large verified Scoreboard is harder to dismiss.

## Contributor Outcomes

Here's what happens to your money. The pool makes money regardless of whether the targets are met (it invests either way). The only question is who gets it.

| Scenario | What happens to your deposit | What happens to your VOTE points | World-side outcome |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Status quo retirement** | Conventional market: `D × {{< var conventional_retirement_15yr_multiple >}}` | N/A | Current trajectory continues. |
| **PRIZE fails** | Depositors divide realized pool: `D × {{< var prize_pool_15yr_multiple >}}` | VOTE points expire worthless. | Status quo branch. |
| **Objectives met** | Deposit routes to VOTE point-holders, not back to you. | Each point pays {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}}. | Everyone gets {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} to {{< var wishonia_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} richer over their lifetime. |

**Worked example: $100 deposit + 2 VOTE points.**

- *Targets missed:* You get back `$100 × {{< var prize_pool_15yr_multiple >}}` = $1,110 from the pool. Your VOTE points pay nothing. You still beat a conventional retirement account (`$100 × {{< var conventional_retirement_15yr_multiple >}}` = $257).
- *Targets met:* Your $100 deposit goes to VOTE point-holders. Your 2 VOTE points pay `2 × {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}} = {{< var vote_2_claims_payout >}}`. Plus you live in a world where people are {{< var treaty_personal_upside_blend >}} to {{< var wishonia_personal_upside_blend >}} richer and diseases get cured.

Two VOTE points turn a small deposit into a large payout. Large depositors beat their retirement account on the failure branch and buy a world with fewer dead people on the success branch.

::: {.callout-note}
## These Numbers Look Large Because the Current Waste Is Large

Your species spends {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}}/year on weapons and {{< var global_government_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}}/year testing which medicines work. That is a {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}}:1 ratio. The "crazy" number is not the solution. It is the ratio that made the solution necessary. Your governments burn {{< var political_dysfunction_global_opportunity_cost_total >}} every year on dysfunction (see [Political Dysfunction Tax](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd) [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]). Large solutions are what large problems look like from the other side.
:::

## What To Do Right Now

The Game needs an institutional host before it can accept PRIZE deposits. In the meantime, you can start playing today:

1. **[Vote on the 1% Treaty.](https://warondisease.org)** 30 seconds. Treaty yes/no, allocation slider with evidence.
2. **Recruit 2 people.** Get two more verified participants onto the Scoreboard.
3. **If you run a foundation or institution:** host the Game. Contact [m@warondisease.org](mailto:m@warondisease.org).

### If You Have Reach

- **Institutions and foundations:** the Game needs a host before PRIZE deposits and the Scoreboard go live. You are the bottleneck. Contact [m@warondisease.org](mailto:m@warondisease.org).
- **Funders:** pick one lane this week and publish the commitment so other participants can coordinate around it.
- **Researchers / builders:** build something this week rather than waiting for perfect certainty.
- **Media:** publish one briefing or story that treats the Scoreboard and futures table as live public infrastructure, not a curiosity.

That is it: vote and recruit. PRIZE deposits begin once an institution hosts the pool. If the Prize fails, you keep your share of the pool (still beats your retirement account). If it succeeds, diseases get cured and everyone gets rich. The first step is small on purpose.

Everything below this line is for readers who want to understand why before they act.

## The Problem Statement

- Your governments are a [misaligned superintelligence](../economics/central-banks.qmd) whose stated objective function is to make you [2% poorer each year](../economics/central-banks.qmd#goal-2-stable-prices-take-2-per-year) and keep you [too busy working to notice](../economics/central-banks.qmd#goal-1-maximum-employment-keep-everyone-busy). Since 1913, they have [printed so much money](../economics/central-banks.qmd) that they've devalued your paycheck by 96%, in order to spend {{< var cumulative_military_spending_fed_era >}} killing {{< var money_printer_war_deaths_nounit >}} people in unpopular wars without asking your permission to have them [@sipri-milex-2024; @crs-war-costs-2010]. The global annual murder budget is {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}}, which is {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} times what governments spend [testing which medicines work](../appendix/global-government-medical-research-spending.qmd).
- The [destructive economy](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] is already {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP, reaches 25% in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_25pct_gdp >}}, and hits the 50% Terminal Parasitic Load Threshold in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}}, where whatever gets created gets looted.
- In 15 years, the status quo path gives you {{< var current_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} median income. A world that stops wasting money on destruction gives you {{< var wishonia_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} ({{< var wishonia_trajectory_lifetime_income_multiplier >}} current lifetime earnings). The gap is that large because waste compounds too: the destructive economy eats {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP now and keeps growing toward 50%, where half of everything created gets looted. Redirect the waste into medicine and R&D instead, and 15 years of compound interest does the rest (see [Political Dysfunction Tax](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd) [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025] for the full waste ledger).
- What that 1% buys: the [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) redirects {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}}/year from military budgets to pragmatic clinical trials. That single reallocation expands trial capacity {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}}, accelerates the drug-disease search space from {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years >}} to {{< var dfda_queue_clearance_years >}}, and averts {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag_lives_saved_nounit >}} deaths (cumulative, over {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag_years >}} of accelerated trial capacity) at {{< var treaty_cost_per_daly_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag >}} per DALY ({{< var treaty_vs_bed_nets_multiplier >}} more cost-effective than anti-malaria bed nets). The {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} is the campaign cost to adopt the treaty; the trials themselves are funded by the redirected military spending, so the direct cost is negative (trials funded *and* 1% fewer bombs) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025].
- The minimum serious first test is that treaty: are humans willing to redirect even 1% from weapons to medicine?

## Why Your Species Needs This Game

Your species has never built a system that measures the two things everyone agrees on (healthy life years and income), publishes the score, and pays whoever moves it. You argue about drug policy without tracking whether fewer people die. You argue about military spending without tracking whether it makes you safer. You argue about healthcare without tracking whether anyone gets healthier. The Game does not resolve these arguments. It makes them irrelevant. Two numbers. Did they move? Pay whoever moved them.

That missing Scoreboard is underneath five specific problems the Game solves at once:

1. **Nobody knows.** Most people have never heard that clinical trials cost {{< var dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient >}} per patient or that 1% of the murder budget would fund all of them.
2. **Everyone thinks they're alone.** Nearly every human would prefer less war and disease. Nobody knows that nearly every other human agrees. So nobody acts.
3. **Nobody can coordinate.** The public has the money ({{< var global_household_wealth_usd >}}) but no way to point it at the same thing at the same time.
4. **Nobody agrees on how.** The Prize does not pick a solution. It pays for outcomes and lets every solution compete.
5. **Nobody knows where to start.** Deposit, register, recruit. That is the entry point.

### 1. Nobody Knows Solutions Exist

Most humans have never heard that pragmatic clinical trials (streamlined trials run inside routine care) cost {{< var dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient >}} per patient (vs. {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient >}} traditional) [@dfda-impact-paper-2025]. That redirecting 1% of the murder budget to medical research gets back {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} times what the campaign costs, in lives saved and health gained [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025]. That {{< var existing_drugs_efficacy_lag_deaths_total_nounit >}} people have already died (since 1962) waiting for drugs that were proven to work but stuck in regulatory queues [@invisible-graveyard-paper-2025]. That you can buy passage of any policy through legal democratic channels.

VOTE points pay people to have a conversation they would otherwise avoid. To recruit someone, you show them the numbers: what military spending costs per life saved vs. clinical trials, how many people died waiting for drugs that already worked, what the economic returns look like. The registration process is the education. The recruitment reward is what makes the education spread.

### 2. Everyone Who Knows Assumes They Are Alone

Your economists call it pluralistic ignorance. Nearly every human would prefer a world without war and treatable disease and an extra {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025]. If every human realized that nearly every other human wants the same thing, it would be done tomorrow. Instead, everyone assumes "this will never happen" because they assume nobody else would agree to it. This is the dumbest reason a civilization has ever continued dying.

Every registration is a person saying "I'm in" where everyone can see it. The Scoreboard counts them all in real time. As the number climbs from thousands to millions to hundreds of millions, "nobody would ever agree to this" stops being an opinion and starts being wrong. You can see that they already did. The [referendum](global-referendum.qmd) does not create demand for not dying. The demand is there. The Scoreboard makes it impossible to pretend it is not.

### 3. The Public Cannot Coordinate Against Concentrated Interests

One of your economists noticed this in 1965 and named it "the logic of collective action" [-@olson1965]. Weapons makers and pharmaceutical monopolies have a lot of money riding on keeping things the way they are, so they organize. The general public has tiny individual stakes and cannot organize back, even though they are the ones dying of untreated diseases and paying for weapons that return {{< var economic_multiplier_military_spending >}} per dollar [@military-spending-economic-multiplier].

Your species identified the exact mechanism by which your governance fails, published it, assigned it in universities, and then continued to be governed by it for sixty years.

But Olson's problem dissolves when people can see each other. The public has the money ({{< var global_household_wealth_usd >}} vs. {{< var concentrated_interest_sector_market_cap_usd >}} held by the opposition [@iab-paper-2025]). It just has no way to act together. The Game is that way: a growing, visible pile of money that gets bigger every time someone clicks a button. No central organizer. No charity. No altruism required. Just millions of people acting in financial self-interest, pointed at the same two numbers.

### 4. Nobody Knows Which Solutions to Implement

There are a million ways to make humans healthier and richer. This manual describes one. It is probably not the best one. It does not need to be. The Game does not pick a solution. It pays for outcomes: healthy life years and income. Anyone, anywhere, who causes either number to rise gets paid.

The Game does not ask anyone to believe this manual is correct. It asks them to believe that less war and disease is worth more than more war and disease, and then it pays them to make it happen.

No committee decides which reforms to fund. A researcher who discovers a cheaper trial design profits. A lobbyist who passes legislation profits. A nonprofit that recruits a million voters profits. {{< var global_coordination_target_supporters_nounit >}} people, each trying to get paid, all pointed at the same two numbers. Your entire species searching for whatever works, instead of arguing about what to search for.

Your species has tried alternatives. "We'll buy it if you build it" (Advance Market Commitments [@kremer2020]) works for vaccines, not systemic reform. Challenge prizes pay the first team across the finish line, then stop. Government procurement funds whatever the person in charge thinks will work, which is the current system, and it is being captured by the people it is supposed to regulate. Prediction markets tell you what will win but do not make it happen. The Game pays for outcomes, publishes the score, and lets anyone challenge the results. Capturing it requires beating every challenger on verified metrics at the same time. Not capture-proof. Capture-expensive.

### 5. Complex Reforms Have No Entry Point

The [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025], FDA reform, wishocratic allocation, making every government on Earth less stupid at the same time: each is a hard sell individually. Each requires explaining an elaborate mechanism to people who have been trained to assume nothing works. The Game is the simple entry point. Put in $1. If nothing works, you keep your money. If the world gets better, VOTE point-holders get paid. One sentence. One decision.

Once someone puts in $1 or earns a VOTE point, they discover the rest through the recruitment process. The treaty. The trial cost data. The allocation evidence. The Game is the door into everything else. "This sounds too complicated" becomes "I put in $1 and either diseases get cured or I keep my money, so why not."

### 6. Nobody Checks Whether the Money Made Things Better or Worse

Your species spent $8 trillion on the War on Terror [@costsofwar2023]. Terrorist attacks went from roughly 1,000 per year to over 17,000 [@global-terrorism-database]. You spent {{< var us_gov_waste_drug_war >}} per year on the War on Drugs for fifty years [@drugpolicyalliance2021]. Overdose deaths went from 6,000 per year to over 100,000 [@cdc-overdose-1980; @cdc-overdose-2023]. Combined scorecard: two programs, $9 trillion spent, both problems roughly 17 times worse. At no point during either program did anyone with budget authority check whether the spending was making the problem better or worse. The data existed. Nobody looked at it. The data did not have a lobbying firm.

This is not incompetence. It is architecture. Each program created a permanent bureaucracy whose continued funding requires the problem to continue existing (see [Path A: Moronia](../futures/moronia.qmd) for the full anatomy of these loops). The DEA needs drug crime. Counter-terrorism needs terrorists. Private prisons have contracts requiring 90% bed occupancy, which means crime dropping is a budget problem. When a policy makes its target problem worse, the responsible agency's budget grows, because a growing problem justifies a growing response. By this logic, the most successful fire department is one that starts fires.

Here's the missing feedback loop. The [Optimitron](../solution/optimocracy.qmd) [@optimocracy-paper-2025] tracks the two numbers (how long people live, how much they earn), publishes them on the Scoreboard, and the [IAB-funded campaign](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025] defunds politicians who ignore them. A policy that spends a trillion dollars and makes the problem 17 times worse shows up as a line going the wrong direction on a public dashboard. The politician who voted for it gets an alignment score. The score is public. Their opponent gets funded. The mechanism does not require anyone to become smarter or more ethical. It requires a Scoreboard that nobody can turn off.

Without the Optimitron, the Prize can measure whether the two numbers moved at year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}, but it cannot tell which policies are dragging them down or which ones moved them up. The Scoreboard tells you the patient's temperature. The Optimitron tells you which of the seventeen drugs you're administering is the one causing the fever.

## The Exponential Math

On Wishonia, if one person tells two people and each of them tells two people, the math handles the rest. Not everyone becomes a recruiter. But "tell two people" gets very large very fast.

| Round | Cumulative people | What that looks like |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 0 | 1 | You |
| 10 | 1,024 | A large lecture hall |
| 15 | 32,768 | A small town |
| 20 | 1,048,576 | A city |
| 25 | 33,554,432 | A country |
| 28 | 268,435,456 | Hundreds of millions; globally visible |
| 32 | 4,294,967,296 | Roughly the modeled global coordination target |
| 33 | 8,589,934,592 | Everyone on Earth |

32 rounds. Not 32 years. 32 rounds. If each round takes a week, that is eight months. If each round takes a month, under three years. One person to world scale in months, not centuries.

"No product in history has achieved 32 rounds of doubling." Correct. The table is the mathematical ceiling, not the operational model. The operational model (see [Treaty Feasibility](../appendix/treaty-feasibility.qmd)) uses R0={{< var chain_effective_r >}} with orbit overlap and realistic attrition. And the actual coordination target is not 8 billion. The Chenoweth threshold ({{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}}) means you need {{< var treaty_campaign_voting_bloc_target_nounit >}} verified participants, not the full planet [@3-5-rule]. That is round 28, not round 33.

Your species already turns out at 50-65% for elections that pay nothing and offer a 1-in-30-million chance of influencing anything [@gelman2012]. This referendum takes 30 seconds on a phone, pays VOTE points on success, and the outcome is "end war and disease and get unimaginably rich." The participation barrier is not "will people do this." It is "will people hear about it." That is what the recruitment incentive solves. Even with heavy dropout, the distance from one person to a globally visible scale is measured in dozens of rounds, not decades (see [the full comparison](#why-this-referendum-beats-your-elections) below).

The target is {{< var global_coordination_target_supporters_nounit >}} people. {{< var global_coordination_target_pct >}} of humanity. VOTE points make recruiting worth doing. The Scoreboard makes the coalition visible. At that scale, the treaty passes well before the pool matures.

| People stop dying | Fewer dead humans per percentage point you shift | {{< var contribution_dalys_per_pct_point_nounit >}} DALYs / {{< var contribution_lives_saved_per_pct_point_nounit >}} lives / {{< var contribution_suffering_hours_per_pct_point_nounit >}} suffering hours per percentage point ([DFDA impact model](../appendix/dfda-impact-paper.qmd)) |

**"Do nothing" is not free.** Your governments already waste {{< var political_dysfunction_tax_per_person_annual >}} per person per year ([Political Dysfunction Tax](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd) [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]). Sitting this out is a bet that everything in the Problem Statement fixes itself. Look at the Problem Statement and decide how confident you are.

::: {.callout-tip}
## This Is a Better Deal Than Any Political Donation in History

Your money stays with you if this fails and goes to VOTE point-holders if it succeeds (see [Contributor Outcomes](#contributor-outcomes)). Either way, it grows at {{< var prize_pool_annual_return >}} annually, reaching {{< var prize_pool_15yr_multiple >}} over {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}} years. Name a political donation that does that.
:::

You do not need to tip the scale by yourself. The stakes are so large that even a tiny nudge is worth real money:

| Your unreimbursed contribution | Break-even probability shift (Treaty floor) | Break-even probability shift (Wishonia) |
|---|---|---|
| `$1K` | `0.0067%` | `0.0019%` |
| `$10K` | `0.067%` | `0.019%` |
| `$100K` | `0.671%` | `0.192%` |
| `$1M` | `6.71%` | `1.92%` |

But does a $1K contribution actually shift probability by 0.0067%? You do not need to be the marginal dollar that tips the scale. You need to believe that more campaign capital makes success more likely than less, which is nearly tautological for political adoption. Those thresholds also treat PRIZE deposits like unreimbursed spending, so they are biased against contributing. They survive heavy skepticism: if you think the per-capita gain is 100x smaller than modeled, the break-even for $1K is still only 0.67%. The math does not require trusting the model. It requires believing the model is not off by more than four orders of magnitude. And the ceiling cost is already bounded: {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} for the 1% Treaty campaign, or {{< var global_political_reform_investment >}} to optimize all public policy globally (see [Problem Statement](#the-problem-statement)).

"Pay people if the outcome happens" and "act once enough others commit" are not new ideas [@tabarrok1998]. The Chenoweth threshold ({{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}}) is the historical floor for when movements become hard to ignore. The RECOVERY trial was run by Oxford and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Every building block is peer-reviewed. The combination is new.

**The free-rider problem has a structural answer.** "VOTE points only pay if the targets are met, so if I don't believe they'll be met, there's no incentive." This assumes VOTE points are the only incentive. They are not. PRIZE deposits beat conventional retirement on the failure branch ({{< var prize_pool_15yr_multiple >}} vs. {{< var conventional_retirement_15yr_multiple >}}). The deposit incentive works regardless of your belief about success. VOTE points add upside on the success branch.

But the deeper answer is that the free-rider problem dissolves when the cost of participation approaches zero. Free-riding is rational when contributing is expensive and the benefit is diffuse. Clicking a button on a phone takes 30 seconds; 50-65% of your species already spends far more effort voting in elections for free. When the cost is 30 seconds and the potential benefit is {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}}, the math does not produce free-riding. It produces "why wouldn't I." Early contributors raise the probability of success, which raises the expected value for later contributors, creating a coordination game that runs on arithmetic rather than altruism.

Delay is not neutral. Each person can only be recruited once, and every month spent waiting gives the status quo more time to compound while the Scoreboard stays smaller than it could be.

The selfish reason to play the Game is not the VOTE payout or the pool return. It is that you personally get {{< var treaty_personal_upside_blend >}} richer in a world where diseases get cured.

## How the Game Spreads

Everything below this point (the lobbying, the treaty campaigns, the clinical trial infrastructure, the [decentralized FDA](../solution/dfda.qmd) [@dfda-spec-paper-2025; @dfda-impact-paper-2025]) is not your job. 4 billion people whose payout depends on curing diseases will attract the lobbyists, researchers, and institutions who know how to cure diseases. You do not need to understand lobbying or clinical trial design. You need to understand that a large enough pile of money pointed at "cure diseases" attracts the people who do.

1. **A host launches the [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd) [@planetary-constitutional-convention-paper-2025].** The manual gets stress-tested. PRIZE deposits begin during this stage. You deposit and recruit.
2. **The referendum opens.** Every depositor learns what the Game is for. The [referendum](global-referendum.qmd) launches: voters set their preferred military-to-health allocation, and every recruiter who brings a verified participant earns VOTE points. The referendum grows because recruitment is rewarded. You keep recruiting.
3. **The Scoreboard climbs.** Votes, treaty support, allocation results, prize pool size, and the two outcome metrics. Each new cohort of participants makes the next cohort easier to convince.
4. **The lobbying campaign starts itself.** Millions of people whose payout depends on treaty passage attract lobbyists, entrepreneurs, and institutions because the pool makes showing up profitable. The [implementation financing](earth-optimization-protocol-v1.qmd) [@earth-optimization-protocol-2025] converts the Scoreboard into political pressure.
5. **Implementation.** Budget authority shifts real resources. Implementers compete to supply the cheapest verified pieces. Again: not your job. Your job was step 1.

Each stage builds the audience for the next. Nobody coordinates this centrally. The incentives coordinate it. For the institutional deployment plan and activation budget, see [Why Your Institution Should Be The Initiating Node](initiating-node-memo.qmd).

## How the Game Moves Money {#how-money-moves-full-mechanism}

Everything the Game exists to produce is either healthy life years or income. Paying separately for budget reallocation or trial enrollment is paying for plumbing that may or may not deliver water. Pay for water.

**Your PRIZE pool trigger.** At year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}: targets met, the pool distributes to VOTE point-holders; targets missed, depositors divide it pro rata.

**Why better ideas win.** The Prize pays for outcomes, not methods. Every proposal in this manual (the treaty, the bonds, the wishocratic fund, the [decentralized FDA](../solution/dfda.qmd) [@dfda-spec-paper-2025; @dfda-impact-paper-2025]) is improvable plumbing. If someone finds a cheaper way to move the two numbers, VOTE point-holders shift recruitment toward it because doing so maximizes their own payout. The two numbers do not change. The plumbing is replaceable. That is the point.

### Why this referendum beats your elections {#why-this-referendum-beats-your-elections}

| Dimension | Your elections | This referendum |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Effort** | Hours in line, research candidates | 30 seconds on a phone |
| **Financial reward** | $0 | {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}} modeled success payout |
| **Your vote matters** | ~1 in 30 million chance of changing the outcome in a typical US national election [@gelman2012] | Direct payout proportional to contribution |
| **Outcome fidelity** | Politician may ignore you after winning | Funds flow to verified implementation |

Your species turns out at 50-65% for elections despite getting paid nothing. This referendum adds a contingent payout, direct attribution, and a public Scoreboard.

**Why more pools make everyone richer.** Your protocol does not need a single pool. It needs a single *metric standard*. Any pool that measures the same two outcomes (healthy life years, median income) and checks that each person is real automatically joins the reward network. A verified person claims proportionally from every participating pool, regardless of which one recorded their vote. Japan launches a pool, the EU launches a pool, the Gates Foundation launches a pool. The combined reward grows with each new entrant. A "competing" pool is actually a deposit. Spending money to "attack" the network is indistinguishable from donating to it. Think of email: you can run your own server; all servers interoperate; running your own extends the network rather than fragmenting it.

**What your protocol must solve.** Six things: (1) verify each person is real and only counts once, (2) register pools, (3) split payouts across pools, (4) add up the Scoreboard, (5) measure the two numbers, (6) pay people. The [protocol specification](../appendix/earth-optimization-prize-protocol.qmd) [@earth-optimization-protocol-2025] has the details.

## Why Everyone's Greed Points the Same Direction

Your politicians care about reelection. Your investors care about returns. Your citizens care about not dying. This is not a design flaw. It is a design constraint. Here is how you work with it instead of against it:

- **Depositors** put money in because they get it back (at {{< var prize_pool_15yr_multiple >}}) if this fails, and buy a world with fewer dead people if it succeeds.
- **Recruiters** recruit because every person they bring in earns them a VOTE point.
- **Entrepreneurs** compete for a giant implementation contract.
- **Politicians** get funded for voting yes and watch their opponents get funded if they vote no (details below).
- **Researchers** compete to prove what works.
- **Citizens** get a 30-second vote that might pay {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}}.

Every participant is doing exactly what they would do anyway, except pointed at diseases instead of each other.

The politician line is the one that requires explanation, because "politicians notice a Scoreboard" has never caused a politician to act against their donors. Here's what converts Scoreboard scale into treaty passage: the [Incentive Alignment Bond](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025]. IABs raise the campaign capital ({{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}}). Investors buy bonds. The campaign passes the treaty. The treaty redirects {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}}/year from military budgets to clinical trials. A management fee on that flow splits three ways: {{< var victory_bond_funding_pct >}} back to investors as a revenue share ({{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} annual returns, which is not a typo), {{< var iab_political_incentive_funding_pct >}} to a SuperPAC that funds treaty-aligned politicians and post-office careers for yes-voters, and {{< var dih_treasury_medical_research_pct >}} to clinical trials through [wishocratic allocation](../solution/wishocracy.qmd) where nobody with money gets to decide where it goes. The investors become the world's most motivated lobbyists for expanding the treaty, because their returns grow with it. The politicians face the same incentive structure that the NRA perfected, pointed at "not dying" instead of "more guns." The loop is self-sustaining: investor greed funds the campaign, campaign greed passes the treaty, treaty revenue feeds investor returns, investor returns fund more campaigns. Nobody has to become good. The money just circulates until diseases stop existing. (For the full mechanism, see [Incentive Alignment Bonds](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025].)

- {{< var global_disease_deaths_daily_nounit >}} humans die every single day from preventable disease ({{< var global_annual_deaths_curable_diseases_nounit >}} this year alone, fifty 9/11s every single day, one Holocaust every 40 days).
- {{< var current_disease_patients_global_nounit >}} people live with chronic disease right now.
- Ongoing genocides and wars are funded by the same {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} military budgets we are asking to redirect 1% of.
- Your governments burn {{< var political_dysfunction_global_opportunity_cost_total >}} every year on dysfunction: health innovation delays, science underfunding, migration restrictions, lead poisoning (see [Political Dysfunction Tax](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd) [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025] for the full ledger). The [destructive economy](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) is already {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP and on track to hit 50% in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}} if nothing changes.

This is not a plan to slightly improve policy. These are instructions for how to stop lighting {{< var political_dysfunction_global_opportunity_cost_total >}} on fire while children die in wars and grandmothers rot from diseases we already know how to fix. Every number below is already modeled, Monte Carlo'd, and linked in the [parameters chapter](../appendix/parameters-and-calculations.qmd).

### 1. "The targets are insanely ambitious"

The Game's targets are the Treaty floor, not a world with optimal governance. HALE of {{< var treaty_projected_hale_year_15 >}} (+{{< var treaty_hale_gain_year_15_nounit >}} healthy years) and median income of {{< var treaty_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} ({{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_multiplier >}} your current lifetime earnings) are what the model produces from a single intervention: redirecting 1% of military spending to clinical trials. A world with optimal governance reaches {{< var wishonia_projected_hale_year_15 >}} HALE and {{< var wishonia_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} median income ({{< var wishonia_trajectory_lifetime_income_multiplier >}} current lifetime earnings; see [GDP Trajectories](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025]). The Prize triggers at the floor, not the ceiling.

The {{< var treaty_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} is compound arithmetic from two mechanisms running simultaneously for 15 years: (1) military-to-R&D redirect ({{< var treaty_annual_funding >}}/year) with a {{< var rd_spillover_multiplier >}} spillover multiplier from your own published studies, and (2) disease-burden recovery (preventable disease currently drags {{< var disease_burden_gdp_drag_pct >}} of GDP; each cure permanently unlocks a slice of that $15 trillion). Year one, the redirect produces twice its value in adjacent-sector growth. Year two, you have last year's redirect plus recovered productivity from diseases the trials identified treatments for. Year three, bigger again. By year five the loop runs on its own output. This is the same compound interest your retirement account uses. The only difference is the return rate (see [GDP Trajectories](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] for the full year-by-year derivation).

Cut every input in half. Cut them in quarters. The model still produces a civilization instead of a collapse, because no plausible adjustment to any single variable eliminates the effect of two compounding mechanisms running simultaneously for 15 years. The math (full Monte Carlo sensitivity in the [parameters chapter](../appendix/parameters-and-calculations.qmd)) shows the Treaty targets are achievable once the 1% redirect clears the drug queue from {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years >}} to {{< var dfda_queue_clearance_years >}} and eliminates the efficacy lag. Anything beyond that (political dysfunction elimination, full governance optimization) pushes toward the Wishonia ceiling and is gravy.

Historical precedent your own species already proved: your grandparents cut military spending by {{< var post_ww2_military_cut_pct >}} in two years after WWII ({{< var us_military_spending_1945_peak_annual_2024usd >}} to {{< var us_military_spending_1947_annual_2024usd >}} in today's dollars) [@us-post-wwii-military-spending-cut]. Factories switched from bombers to Cadillacs. The economy exploded into the greatest boom in human history [@us-post-wwii-gdp-growth-8-pct]. "But the military-industrial complex didn't exist in 1945." Correct. That is why we budgeted {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} instead of $25M, and why [Incentive Alignment Bonds](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025] create a bondholder class whose income scales with treaty expansion. The MIC has a lobby. The IAB creates a counter-lobby with {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns. The difference between 1945 and 2026 is not that reallocation is harder. It is that you need to buy your way past the people who profit from the status quo. The budget accounts for this. They managed {{< var post_ww2_military_cut_pct >}} during demobilization and built the middle class. We are asking for 1%.

I have noticed your smartest humans spend more time explaining why solutions will not work than explaining why {{< var global_annual_deaths_curable_diseases_nounit >}} annual deaths should continue. The same humans will not mention that your species currently spends {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} times more on weapons than testing which medicines work, because that number is familiar and therefore not interesting. You are being asked for 1% and acting like someone suggested disbanding the army during an invasion. Either the human genome degraded significantly since your grandparents managed to redirect {{< var post_ww2_military_cut_pct >}} of military spending to useful things, or someone is making a lot of money telling you this is impossible.

### 2. "Treaties never work"

Your species has already banned entire weapons industries multiple times, without any greed-powered [Incentive Alignment Bonds](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd):

- Biological Weapons Convention (1972/1975): 187 countries outlawed an entire category of WMD.
- Chemical Weapons Convention (1993): 193 countries banned chemical weapons production and stockpiles.
- Ottawa Treaty (1997): 164 countries banned landmines. One woman with a phone and a coalition of NGOs did it in 14 months, despite major military powers opposing it [@icbl-ottawa-treaty].
- Cluster Munitions Convention (2008): same story, two years [@cluster-munitions-convention-2008].

None of these needed Victory Incentive Alignment Bonds or {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns. They passed because enough people got sufficiently annoyed. The 1% Treaty is easier: it keeps 99% of every military budget intact, the relative power balance unchanged, and it bribes everyone with massive personal upside. The [Treaty Feasibility](../appendix/treaty-feasibility.qmd) appendix shows historical campaign costs of $25-50M; we budgeted {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} with a benefit-cost ratio exceeding {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} [@cost-of-change-paper-2025].

A human trying to sound smart might explain why the treaty with financial incentives is less likely to work than the ones without them.

### 3. "Goodhart's Law"

On your planet, there is a tradition of raising Goodhart's Law at this point in the conversation. It is how your species signals analytical sophistication without proposing a better pair of metrics. The concern is not that HALE and median income are bad metrics. The concern is that any metric with hundreds of trillions riding on it will be gamed. Fair. Here is why it is harder than it sounds.

Mortality is binary and hard to fake across millions of people. You either died or you did not. Hospitals, insurance claims, mortality registries, and satellite-derived economic indicators all have to agree. Median income requires improving the middle of the distribution, not just the top; you cannot game it by making billionaires richer.

The [protocol](../appendix/earth-optimization-prize-protocol.qmd) [@earth-optimization-prize-protocol-paper-2025] specifies three structural defenses: (1) methodology lock-in at baseline, so any WHO or World Bank methodology change requires re-baselining and resets the improvement clock; (2) minimum population coverage (data must represent at least 80% of the global population, so you cannot improve the number by excluding the sick or poor); and (3) decentralized survey cross-checks using the voter base itself, adding a methodology-independent data stream collected directly from millions of humans. One person lying has approximately zero effect on the median. This is statistics, not voting.

The [Optimitron](../solution/optimocracy.qmd) [@optimocracy-paper-2025] adds five independent measurement sources (census, federal reserve, labor statistics, academic institutions, decentralized citizen surveys) where corrupting all simultaneously requires bribing five institutions that hate each other. The adversarial challenge window means anyone who catches gaming can post a bond, present evidence, and claw back the payout.

I have been watching your planet for 81 years and have not heard a better pair of terminal metrics for human welfare proposed. If you have one, the protocol is [open source](https://github.com/wishonia/earth-optimization-instructions). The alternative is the Terminal Parasitic Load trajectory: destructive economy at 50% of GDP in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}} while {{< var global_annual_deaths_curable_diseases_nounit >}} die yearly.

### 4. "The implementation is impossibly complex"

I have noticed humans list implementation requirements to prove something is hard, then use things more complex than every item on the list before breakfast. The six capabilities the protocol must solve all already exist at scale:

| Capability needed | What already does this |
|:---|:---|
| Identity layer (one person, one vote) | KYC bank accounts. Your species verifies identity billions of times daily for far less important reasons than curing disease. |
| Pool registry | Investment funds. Vanguard manages $9T across millions of accounts. A prize pool is a fund with a conditional payout trigger. |
| Cross-pool claim settlement | Interbank settlement. SWIFT processes $5T/day across 200+ countries. Splitting a pool pro rata is simpler than a wire transfer. |
| Scoreboard aggregation | Election results dashboards. Every democracy already aggregates and publishes vote counts in real time. |
| Measure the two numbers | WHO and World Bank. They already publish HALE and median income annually. That IS the measurement. |
| Claim mechanics | Dividend payments. Corporations pay billions of shareholders quarterly. Paying VOTE point-holders once is simpler. |

The Game does not require inventing anything. It is a survey where you prove you are a real person, and a savings account that pays out if enough people convince their governments to stop wasting money. Legally, it is an escrow account with a payout trigger, not a security. The referendum could be a ballot measure; elections already exist. Enforcement: the treaty IS the enforcement, exactly like every other treaty your species has signed.

Your species built a system that moves $5 trillion across borders every day, verifies 8 billion identities, and counts 4 billion votes in elections. You are telling me you cannot build a survey with a savings account attached.

### 5. "The 17.4% return is too good to be true"

The {{< var prize_pool_annual_return >}} is not a promise. It is transparent arithmetic from four independently sourced components: (1) {{< var venture_gross_return >}} venture capital gross return (Cambridge Associates 25-year pooled IRR), (2) {{< var scale_compression_factor >}} scale compression drag (explicitly modeled for 15x market expansion; i.e., the model already penalizes itself for the skeptic's concern about diminishing returns), (3) +{{< var wishocratic_crowd_alpha >}} crowd allocation alpha ({{< var crowd_decision_accuracy >}} crowd accuracy vs. {{< var expert_decision_accuracy >}} for expert fund managers [@surowiecki-2004]; the S&P SPIVA scorecard confirms 88% of actively managed large-cap funds underperformed the S&P 500 over 15 years [@spiva2023]), and (4) +{{< var home_bias_alpha >}} from eliminating home-country bias (70+ countries each overweight domestic assets, missing global diversification; IMF/Vanguard estimate 0.3-1.5% annual drag). The structural advantage is not a feedback loop or a hope. It is arithmetic from removing fees, removing the accreditation wall, and letting crowds allocate. See [Wishocratic Investment Fund](../economics/wishocratic-investment-fund.qmd) for the full derivation.

### 6. "272% returns is a scam"

To anyone in finance, "{{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} annual returns" sounds like a red flag. Good. It should sound unusual. It is not a market return. It is a political-risk premium. The math: the treaty redirects {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}}/year. A {{< var victory_bond_funding_pct >}} management fee = {{< var victory_bond_annual_payout >}}/year. The campaign costs {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}}. {{< var victory_bond_annual_payout >}} / {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} = {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}}. The appropriate comparison is not the S&P 500. It is the return on any binary political bet that hits: lobby for a policy, the policy passes, you capture a percentage of the resulting revenue flow. Lobbying returns routinely exceed 100:1 when they work [@lobbying-roi-calc]. The 272% is contingent on the treaty actually passing, which is the hard part. The transparency is the defense: every number is disclosed, not hidden. And the bondholders become the world's most motivated lobbyists for expanding the treaty, because their returns grow with it. The mechanism that looks like a red flag is the mechanism that makes your treaty durable. (For the full derivation, see [Incentive Alignment Bonds](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025].)

### 7. "The VOTE payout assumes $70 trillion flows into the pool"

It does not assume that. It calculates the ceiling. The {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}} per VOTE point is what happens if the entire global retirement asset base ({{< var global_retirement_assets >}}) compounds through the wishocratic fund over {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}} years. That is a potential maximum, not the opening ask.

| Pool participation | Pool size (15-year compounded) | VOTE payout per point |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 0.1% of retirement assets ($70B) | $777B | ~$194 |
| 1% ($700B) | $7.8T | ~$1,940 |
| 10% ($7T) | $77.7T | ~$19,400 |
| 100% ($70T) | $777T | {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}} |

At 1% participation, a VOTE point pays about $1,940. At 10%, $19,400. The pool does not need to reach $70T for the Game to be worth playing. It needs to reach the size where the recruitment incentive exceeds the effort of telling two people. That threshold is low.

### 8. "The 604:1 ratio cherry-picks the denominator"

The {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}}:1 compares government military spending ({{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}}) to government clinical trial spending ({{< var global_government_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}}). Government-to-government. The treaty redirects government money, so this is the correct like-for-like comparison.

"But industry funds 90% of clinical trials." Yes. And industry only tests drugs that can be patented and sold for high prices. Off-patent cures, orphan diseases, repurposed generics, and every disease that does not affect enough rich people get zero industry funding. The {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}}:1 measures the gap that only government can close. Even if you include all clinical trial spending ({{< var global_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}}), the ratio is still {{< var military_to_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}}:1. That is not a rebuttal. That is a confession. (See [Global Government Medical Research Spending](../appendix/global-government-medical-research-spending.qmd) for the full accounting.)

"Political impossibility" is a capital allocation problem, not a physics problem. |
| "Does this require trusting one institution?" | No. A credible host can initiate the network, but it should not be the root of trust. The rules, contracts, interfaces, and measurement layers should remain open, forkable, and replaceable so another host can continue the process if the first one fails. |
| "Does hosting mean endorsing the current manual?" | No. The host endorses the process, not the draft. See [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd). |
| "I'd lose my $1" | On failure, depositors divide the realized pool pro rata. On success, the deposit funds the pool by design. The selfish case is that the rest of your life got much larger than the dollar you put in. |
| "Can I sell my claim?" | Not inside the protocol. PRIZE stays with the depositor's verified account until resolution. VOTE stays with the verified recruiter who earned it. Private contracts can exist outside the protocol, like assigning future royalties, but the protocol does not broker or enforce them. |
| "Why can't PRIZE be withdrawn early?" | Because a redeem-anytime exit right would let depositors drain the pool as success became more likely. The Game only works if the capital remains committed until the measurement date. |
| "What if I die or lose access?" | Claims belong to a verified account, not a fragile device. The system needs account recovery, beneficiary designation, and lawful successor control so a 15-year claim does not disappear because you lost your phone or your heirs need to prove who they are. |
| "Nobody else will participate" | That IS the problem the Game exists to solve. Your deposit is the proof that someone does. The Scoreboard makes everyone else's participation visible. |
| "I don't understand the mechanism" | You do not need to. [Vote](https://warondisease.org), recruit 2 people. |
| "Why can't VOTE points be traded?" | Tradability would buy liquidity but invert the signal: outsiders could buy coalition credit without doing coalition work. The public signal this design relies on is simpler: verified participant count, referendum growth, and a visible pool of committed capital. |

Your mechanism does not need participants to be wise. It needs them to be self-interested, impatient, and capable of reading a scoreboard. The whole thing is [open source](https://github.com/wishonia/earth-optimization-instructions).

While you were reading this chapter, approximately {{< var global_disease_deaths_per_minute_nounit >}} humans permanently stopped every minute. Not because the solution was too complicated. Because nobody [voted](https://warondisease.org).

Four treaties banned entire weapons industries without paying anyone to sign them. This one pays people. I find it interesting that the version with financial incentives draws more objections than the versions without.

The math does not require every reader. It requires enough readers to fill a [scoreboard](https://warondisease.org).
